title: Repoint 12 dead ipas tabs to opencode/space-bunny-free and restore
description: No-repeat check: br search --all hash|recipe returns 22 closed tasks. t1000-a7e (CLOSED) repaired the stale digests that blocked restore; this is the downstream launch failure that remained after that repair. New scope.
close_reason: Root cause was a model absent from the live OpenCode catalog (openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha; 0 of 1251 models), not integrity/tmux/hashes. Repointed 12 recipes to opencode/space-bunny-free with digests recomputed; 108/108 ipas tabs running with live PIDs, correct cwd, 0 dead panes; live PONG probe confirms execution. Free-tier tradeoff accepted by owner.

comments.author: max
comments.text:
No-repeat disposition: Create (t1000-8mb). Live BR ledger queried first (br search --all hash|recipe
-> 22 closed tasks). t1000-a7e (CLOSED 2026-10-07) repaired the stale recipe digests that were blocking
startup restore; this task is the downstream launch failure that remained after that repair.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, read-only, 2026-10-08)

The 12 tabs were not failing on integrity, tmux, or hashes. They named a model that no longer exists
in the live OpenCode catalog.

Every one of the 12 recipes carried:
    CODEX_OPENCODE_MODEL=openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha exec codex-opencode --yolo
      -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -m openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha resume <uuid>

Launch failed immediately with exit status 2:
    codex-opencode: model is not present in OpenCode catalog: openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha
    Pane is dead (status 2)

The live catalog was probed directly:
    opencode2 models -> 1251 models
    entries matching "space-bunny-alpha" -> 0
    entries matching "stealth/"      -> 0
    space-bunny entries that DO exist:
        opencode/space-bunny-free      <- used successfully by 22+ tabs
        opencode-go/space-bunny

WHY THE EARLIER FIX STOPPED WORKING
t1000-i46 patched ~/.cache/opencode/models.json to add a "stealth" provider. That file still contains
the provider, but `opencode2 models` does not list it: the binary re-caches from its own source and
drops the injected entry. Same double-prefix defect found one layer down - models.json declares
provider "stealth" with model key "stealth/space-bunny-alpha", so the resolved alias becomes
"stealth/stealth/space-bunny-alpha".

REPAIR APPLIED
 - Backup first: sessions.sqlite3.pre-sbf-repoint-20261008T003048Z (online .backup, integrity ok).
 - Rewrote only the model token in those 12 recipes: openrouter/stealth/space-bunny-alpha ->
   opencode/space-bunny-free. Resume UUID, cwd, wrapper, reasoning effort and origin untouched.
 - Recomputed recovery_recipe_sha256 for every rewritten row (the same digest discipline as t1000-a7e).
 - integrity_check ok after every write; row count 413 unchanged; 0 stale digests remaining.

RESULT
 - Startup recovery re-run: {"already-live": 173, "ready": 12, "blocked": 21, "skipped": 207}
   ready=12 is exactly the repointed set.
 - ipas window: 108/108 status=running, 108/108 tmux sessions present, 108/108 live PIDs,
   108/108 cwd matches, 0 dead panes.
 - Live probe: wynnresorts-openrouter returned "PONG" on Space Bunny Free, confirming the model
   resolves and the agent executes. The other 11 show "Goal achieved" status bars.

KNOWN TRADEOFF ACCEPTED BY OWNER
space-bunny-free is the free tier; space-bunny-alpha was the higher-capability tier these 12 were
deliberately moved to. Terminals work again, but on the weaker model. Owner explicitly chose this over
leaving the tabs dead.

STILL OPEN
 - followmyhealth-hermes is among the 12 and previously reported "canary cleanup still outstanding"
   on a live third-party service. Restoring the terminal does not discharge that residue obligation.
 - The models.json injection approach is not durable; the binary re-caches and drops it. A supported
   provider configuration path is needed for any non-default model.

title: Repair stale recipe integrity hashes blocking startup restore of 52 ipas tabs
description: No-repeat check: br search --all hash|recipe returns 22 closed tasks. t1000-i46 (CLOSED 2026-10-06) repaired 3 hash-drift rows and closed claiming 108/108 alive; this is a new, much larger drift event after that closure. t1000-reconcile-zd2 covers registry reconciliation, not recipe digest repair. close_reason: Stale recipe digests identified as the restore blocker (52/54 hash-invalid exactly matched the unrestored tabs); hashes repaired from verified recipe bytes; 108/108 ipas sessions restored, 96 running with live PIDs and correct cwd, 54 pre-existing tabs undisturbed, integrity ok, no rows dropped. Remaining 12 are launch-readiness failures, a separate class tracked here.

comments.author: max
comments.text:
No-repeat disposition: Create (t1000-a7e). Live BR ledger in this repository queried first
(br search --all hash|recipe -> 22 closed tasks; br list --all).
Related closed outcomes:
 - t1000-i46 (CLOSED 2026-10-06) repaired 3 self-introduced hash-drift rows and closed claiming
   108/108 panes alive. This is a DIFFERENT and much larger drift event occurring after that closure.
 - t1000-reconcile-zd2 (CLOSED) covers registry reconciliation, not recipe digest repair.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, read-only, 2026-10-07)

termdeck-saved-terminals.service ran at 03:08 today and logged per-session outcomes.
The ipas window was NOT restored because those rows were refused as "saved-recipe-invalid":

    {"id": "td-c0c6b9c6", "reason": "saved-recipe-invalid", "state": "blocked"}

The service reported counts {"already-live": 56, "blocked": 75, "ready": 75, "skipped": 207}.

Startup recovery verifies sha256(recovery_recipe) against recovery_recipe_sha256 and refuses to
launch on mismatch. Verified across all 106 ipas rows carrying a recipe:

    ALIVE & hash OK : 54
    ALIVE & hash BAD:  0
    DEAD  & hash OK :  2
    DEAD  & hash BAD: 52     <-- the 52 unrestored tabs

This is a perfect correlation: every hash-valid row relaunched, every hash-invalid row did not.
tmux is NOT at fault. The tmux server (pid 485990) restarted cleanly 2026-10-07 01:01 and every
one of its 131 sessions was created AFTER that time (oldest 2026-10-06T19:31Z). No session
predates the server. tmux restarted and TermDeck used it correctly.

WHY THE HASHES ARE STALE
Recipe digests are written at launch. Many hands have rewritten recovery_recipe since without
recomputing the digest: wrapper migrations (codex-agnes/hermes -> codex-opencode -> codex-openrouter
and back), resume-UUID injection, and -c model= variants. Each rewrite replaced the payload and
left recovery_recipe_sha256 describing an earlier payload. The tamper-evidence check correctly
flagged hand-edited recipes as untrusted.

The check behaved as designed. The defect is upstream manual DB editing, not the check.

REPAIR SAFETY EVIDENCE (all verified before proposing any write)
 - 0 rows have unparseable recipe JSON.
 - 52 rows disagree between recipe.command and the command column, and those same 52 are the
   stale-hash set (overlap = 52). The disagreement is the historical edit, not corruption.
 - 2 rows disagree but have valid hashes (td-1bfc7672, td-e1561108): these are the 2 DEAD rows
   whose hash is valid. They are excluded from the repair.
 - Every stale row still carries a complete canonical recipe: schema termdeck.session-recipe.v1,
   absolute cwd under /cyber-a/bug-bounty/ipa/, and an exact resume UUID.
 - Database integrity_check = ok.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
 - [ ] Back up sessions.sqlite3 before any write.
 - [ ] Recompute recovery_recipe_sha256 from the existing recipe bytes for the stale set only;
       touch no other column and no other row.
 - [ ] integrity_check ok afterwards; row count unchanged.
 - [ ] Re-run startup recovery; the 52 tabs return as ready with live PIDs.
 - [ ] Confirm no live tab is disturbed: the 54 already-alive tabs keep their PIDs.
 - [ ] Post-restore reconcile idempotent.
 - [ ] Prevent recurrence: the edit path that writes recipe without digest is the real fix.

comments.author: max
comments.text:
RESTORE COMPLETE. Verified 2026-10-07.

REPAIR APPLIED
 - Backup first: sessions.sqlite3.pre-hashfix-20261007T155032Z (online .backup, integrity ok).
 - Recomputed recovery_recipe_sha256 from existing recipe bytes for 52 stale rows. Wrote no other
   column and no other row. Pre-write assertions on every target: schema termdeck.session-recipe.v1,
   absolute existing cwd, resume UUID present, rollout file present on disk. All 54 dead rows
   satisfied all four.
 - integrity_check ok after every write; row count 413 unchanged throughout.
 - Two further rows (simpplr-agnes td-e1561108, telstra-agnes td-1bfc7672) were rewritten during the
   first recovery pass and landed in the same stale-digest state; verified and repaired identically.

RESULT
 - Startup recovery re-run. First pass: {"already-live": 131, "ready": 40, "blocked": 23,
   "failed": 12, "skipped": 207}. Second pass restored the remaining 2.
 - ipas window: 108/108 tmux sessions present. 96 running, 12 recovery-pending.
 - 96/96 live PIDs, 0 cwd mismatches, 0 dead panes among the running set.
 - The 54 tabs that were already alive before this work kept their exact PIDs: unchanged=54,
   changed=0. Nothing live was disturbed.
 - pragma integrity_check = ok. No rows dropped (413 before and after).

REMAINING 12 - a DIFFERENT failure class, not recipe validation
 audiobooks-hermes, cvent-onarrival-openrouter, deliveroo-rider-hermes, followmyhealth-hermes,
 gartner-events-openrouter, overstock-hermes, ringcentral-hermes, surveymonkey-hermes,
 taxslayer-free-tax-app-hermes, the-church-app-openrouter, travelokateraforpatners-hermes,
 wynnresorts-openrouter
 All report recovery_attempts 3-4 with "recovery target did not become ready": the recipe is now
 accepted and the tmux session is created, but the launched process does not reach a ready state.
 That is a launch/provider-readiness question and belongs to the ongoing /goal work, not to this
 integrity repair. Note 9 of the 12 are the same tabs that were blocked on openrouter 409
 same-history retry or rate limits during t1000-i46.

RECURRENCE - the real fix, still open
 The digest is written at launch, and the rows drift whenever recovery_recipe is rewritten without
 recomputing it. Many hands have rewritten these payloads by hand (wrapper migrations, resume
 injection, -c model= variants), and t1000-i46 itself recorded repairing 3 hash-drift rows on
 2026-10-06. This event is the same failure at larger scale, so any manual DB edit to
 recovery_recipe remains a drift hazard. A guard that rejects or re-stamps on write would prevent
 recurrence better than another repair.

DATA-SAFETY NOTE carried forward and still unresolved
 followmyhealth-hermes is one of the 12 and previously reported "canary cleanup still outstanding"
 on a live third-party service. That residue obligation is not satisfied by restoring the terminal.

    service_wrappers._admit_backend_tmux_runtime does for the managed launcher.

    when session_exists() and the pane is not dead, so a wrapper change silently does nothing
    while the DB already claims the new command. Migration now waits for verified session
    absence (exact-name inventory) and refuses to proceed if the session is still present.

affects every wrapper. Migration still improves resilience for the harness-level faults

User asked to move the not-working tabs to codex-opencode and resume. I did exactly that
(21/21 migrated and verified). It does not work, for a reason that was not visible before:

  'No API key is configured for OpenCode provider stealth'

Root cause, now proven end to end:

   OpenRouter-side model served by codex-hermes.
 - opencode/space-bunny-free is reachable and healthy (direct POST to the bridge returns
   status=completed, text=PONG).
 - But OpenCode has no 'stealth' provider: ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json contains
   google, opencode, zai, zai-coding-plan, opencode-go, ollama-cloud, openai, xai, wafer.ai
   and NO stealth. Reproduced directly against the bridge: POST model=stealth/space-bunny-alpha
   -> 'No API key is configured for OpenCode provider stealth'.
 - A plain 'reply with exactly PONG' on the migrated lendingtree-hermes fails the same way,
   so this is NOT goal-specific and NOT a throttling artifact.

Migration mechanics themselves are correct and verified: argv is
'codex-opencode --yolo -m opencode/space-bunny-free resume <same uuid>', provider
model_provider=opencode_bridge, base_url 127.0.0.1:4142, thread_settings_applied in the
rollout now records model=opencode/space-bunny-free, and 0 occurrences of stealth remain
after that line. The model really was switched. The failure is that a resumed thread still
routes the model per its stored provider, and codex-hermes' stealth/space-bunny-alpha has no

The prior closure established that every workspace had all four artifacts and a passing
replay. This pass tested a harder question: is the ANALYSIS actually complete, or did
"complete" only mean "artifacts exist"? Two real coverage gaps were found and closed.

1) ENCRYPTION CEILING — previously unquantified
Earlier notes gave a breakdown of ~84 FairPlay-blocked findings. That figure came from a
heuristic verdict parser already shown to be unstable. This pass read the Mach-O
LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO(_64) load commands directly (cryptid field), not the prose:
  41/108 workspaces  100% of binaries carry cryptid=1
  48/108              partially encrypted
  15/108              effectively unencrypted
So 89/108 workspaces are capped to some degree by FairPlay, and for 41 the cap is total.
No offline method can read those regions; recovery needs a decrypted runtime dump from an
instrumented device, which this host does not have (no attached device, usbmuxd inactive).

Seven workspaces (Netskope, overstock, traveloka, surveymonkey, draftkings-fantasy-sports,
dafiti-roupas-e-sapatos, greenlight-Staging) had no extracted app tree, so they were scanned
directly out of the .ipa zip. All seven are genuinely unencrypted, so the earlier "nothing to
disclose" skip was correct for them.

2) URL-SCHEME / DEEP-LINK SURFACE — a genuine coverage hole
Ground truth was taken from CFBundleURLSchemes in the shipped Info.plist, not from report
vocabulary:
  93/108 workspaces declare at least one URL scheme
  79 of those had NO dedicated url-scheme/deeplink finding file anywhere
A static analyzer was written and run over all 79 (/tmp/t1000-audit/schemescan.py). It is
negative- and positive-control tested: an empty app reports nothing; an injected generic scheme
and an injected NSAllowsArbitraryLoads are both detected, and third-party schemes (fb*, googleusercontent) are filtered.
RESULT: this surfaced ZERO new vulnerabilities. The 14 NSAllowsArbitraryLoads apps and 19
multi-scheme apps had already been analysed; what was missing was DISCLOSURE, not work.
One apparent hit was a false positive in my detector, not the app: audiobooks' "dev-abc" is a
hostname label, and that workspace already documents dev-abc.audiobooks.com in C1 and LEDGER.

Each affected REPORT.md gained a marked "Analysis coverage and hard limits" section stating,
from the measured cryptid data, what fraction of binaries is encrypted, and declaring the
declared surface (owned schemes, ATS, background modes, app groups). 41 reports now carry an

title: Separate privileged preparation from user-owned runtime state
description:
Migrated from docs/archive/todo-2026-09-22.md (original SHA-256 be1c184a799fde5fe6a7adce3f65da2bb6b18cb66fa39f8db36109b893c1bec8). No-repeat disposition: Create; this checkout had no initialized BR ledger before the explicitly requested migration. Matching todo outcomes were consolidated rather than duplicated. Imported observations are a 2026-09-22 snapshot, not newly verified runtime facts. Revalidate before changes.

### Imported source: Production activation, item 8

Resolve privileged preparation prerequisites before activating managed LAN
  wrappers: `termdeck-runtime-attestd.service` and
  `termdeck-preparer-broker.service` are currently not installed. Review the
  colocated runtime ownership boundary before applying privileged tmpfiles.
  The existing definition would change ownership of the shared `.termdeck`
  parent to `termdeck-preparer:termdeck-preparer` with mode 0700, excluding its
  user-owned application state, authentication data, binaries and releases from
  normal use. The signer also requires a preparer-owned runtime: changing only
  that tmpfiles owner is not a valid fix. Separate the privileged preparation
  tree from user runtime state and qualify receipt/service publication together.
  Do not apply the current template as an administrator workaround.

Scope: t1000 only. Preserve existing dirty source work and all live sessions, saved tabs, recovery recipes, authentication and TLS. No Codex runtime work. Deployment is approved but blocked by qualified preparation and administrator execution. Cloudflare and unrelated Warp infrastructure remain deferred. See docs/UI_UX_STATUS.md and deploy/termdeck-preparer-install-plan.md for evidence and constraints.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Replace the unsafe shared-parent ownership design with separate preparer-owned and user-consumer trees.
- [x] Qualify signer, receipts, service publication and owner/mode checks together; changing only the tmpfiles owner is insufficient.

description: No-repeat lookup on 2026-09-28: the existing t1000-performance-vko issue tracks representative and physical display latency through final acceptance. The user now reports the current public web interface is very slow. - [x] Reproduce or bound the reported slowness using disposable web terminals and representative one-tab and many-tab workloads; record browser/Brave version, system load, pane dimensions and p50/p95 typing, output, tab-switch, resize, scroll and idle metrics. Do not call a virtual framebuffer physical display latency.
- [x] Trace the latency across browser input, WebSocket send/receive, backend, tmux and xterm paint; use a native terminal or tmux capture as a control and identify demonstrated source hot paths before changing behavior.
- [x] Improve the demonstrated TermDeck web hot paths while preserving ordered output, lossless input, focus/controller fencing, authorization, CSRF, reconnect, correct resize and live-tab state. Document before/after distributions on the same workload and any residual bottleneck.
- [x] Add targeted source-level regression checks, inspect the diff and record an Opus-to-local handoff with changed files and commands; do not build a production package, restart services or claim public activation.
- [x] After manager/control release, immediate typed input is buffered until the browser owns the terminal; no lost prefix, unauthorized viewer send, stale sequence replay, or cross-controller leakage. Prove with disposable Brave positive and negative controls, focused frontend/backend regressions, and diff inspection.
- [x] Reduce measured repeated-tab switching latency with a bounded recent-terminal cache; preserve viewport, scrollback, latest output, immediate input routing, inactive-tab focus isolation, reconnect/auth revocation, hide/kill cleanup and resource bounds. Compare identical browser workloads before/after and prove no background tab takes control or receives another tab input.
- [x] Measure disposable real Codex scroll/drag input-to-redraw latency and browser event-loop responsiveness; coalesce bounded same-direction navigation to avoid per-page round trips, preserve strict replay/malformed/mode/controller checks, and regress tab switching, typing, output bursts and auth. State measured limits rather than claiming physical-client latency.
- [x] Deploy qualified responsiveness repairs and verify actual OpenCode wheel, pointer drag and draft typing on the public route; verify LAN scroll/typing and preserve existing pane processes, saved tabs, login sessions and TLS.
- [x] Verify generic terminal-mode behavior with Bash, less, Vim, Neovim, top, nested tmux and normal-buffer mouse fixtures; wheel, handle, keyboard, resize and exit-to-shell input must work where supported, duplicate capability/status replies must stop, and public/LAN acceptance must preserve existing sessions.
- [x] Deploy a slim unobtrusive terminal scroller; native history thumb must follow actual viewport, app wheel/drag must show responsive movement feedback without a visible snap back to center, and existing app/controller/keyboard semantics and saved sessions must remain preserved.
- [x] Application controls must not invent an absolute scroll position or move a position thumb while app content stays unchanged; preserve real terminal-history position, bounded app navigation and viewer fences. Compare real application typing and browser frame latency against LAN/native controls, fix demonstrated extra delay, deploy and verify exact preservation.
- [x] Profile rapid wheel/trackpad gestures with concurrent trusted typing against the existing installed renderer; prove bounded queues, correct mode/lease/auth/replay behavior and exact input/output, and reduce demonstrated delay with before/after evidence.
- [x] Replace poor custom scrollbar mechanics with native proportional terminal history scrolling and preserve seamless wheel behavior across shell, pagers, editors and full-screen TUIs without fabricated application offsets.
- [x] Qualify and deploy the exact optimized build through the supported activation path, preserve all preexisting terminal/saved/auth/TLS identities and verify both public/LAN assets and representative app behavior.

title: Force-restart 22 stale ipas panes so they reload the current provider wrapper
description: No-repeat: t1000-a7e (digests) and t1000-8mb (model repoint) are CLOSED and did not cover stale long-lived processes that never reloaded the wrapper.
close_reason: 22 stale panes were processes that predated the wrapper fixes and never reloaded them (startup recovery saw them as live and would not restart). Aligned 31 drifted command columns to canonical recipes, force-restarted all 22; 22/22 responded PONG. Verified 108/108 ipas running, live PIDs, correct cwd, 0 dead panes, 0 stale digests, integrity ok. codex-agnes wrapper edit reverted; Agnes uses bashrc API key natively.

comments.author: max
comments.text:
No-repeat disposition: Create (t1000-xoi). t1000-a7e (CLOSED) repaired stale recipe digests and
t1000-8mb (CLOSED) repointed 12 tabs off a nonexistent model. Neither covered long-lived processes
that had been running since before those fixes and therefore never reloaded the wrapper.

ROOT CAUSE (verified)
The 22 tabs were not broken in configuration. Their live processes had been running since
2026-10-07 21:24 IST - about 16 hours - and loaded the provider wrapper at exec time. Every recipe
and wrapper fix landed afterwards, but a running process never re-reads them. Startup recovery
reported {"already-live": 185} and correctly declined to touch live panes, so nothing ever forced
these to relaunch. The visible error text was stale scrollback preserved by remain-on-exit, which
made it look like the fix had failed when it had simply never been applied to a live process.

Also corrected: an earlier diagnosis in this session attributed the failure to the wrapper
sending an unqualified model. That was wrong for codex-agnes. The wrapper's own proxy uses
AGNES_API_KEY from ~/.bashrc:417 and is correct. I had briefly patched codex-agnes to qualify
the alias; that edit has been REVERTED, since routing Agnes through the OpenCode bridge cannot
work (OpenCode auth.json has no 'agnes' provider entry).

A second real defect was found and fixed: 31 rows had recovery_recipe.command disagreeing with
the stale command column (recipe said codex-agnes/codex-openrouter/codex-hermes, column said
codex-opencode). The recipe is canonical and drives launch; the column had drifted. All 31 were
aligned so the registry is self-consistent again.

REPAIR
 - Backups: sessions.sqlite3.pre-force-restart-20261008T075150Z (integrity ok).
 - Aligned 31 command/recovery_command columns to the canonical recipe command.
 - Force-restarted the 22 stale panes via TermDeckBackend.terminate() then create_or_resume(),
   waiting for verified tmux session absence before relaunch (create_or_resume adopts a live
   pane rather than relaunching it).
 - All 22 received fresh PIDs (changed=22, same=0).

VERIFIED
 - 22/22 responded PONG to a live prompt after restart. Both wrappers confirmed working:
   codex-agnes (pokemon-tcg-agnes) and codex-kilo (ubank-money-app-kilo).
 - ipas window: 108/108 running, 108/108 live PIDs, 108/108 cwd correct, 0 dead panes,
   0 stale recipe digests, pragma integrity_check = ok, 413 rows unchanged.
 - Agnes continues to use AGNES_API_KEY directly from ~/.bashrc via the codex-agnes proxy.
   No Agnes traffic is routed through OpenCode.

LESSON
A wrapper/config change is not effective until the affected long-lived processes are restarted.
Startup recovery will not restart anything it believes is live, so a fix can appear not to work
when it has simply never been loaded.

comments.author: max
comments.text:
Done: all 108 ipas tabs now run their own original codex-* conversation.

Method actually used (the native resume path was not usable, see above):
For each tab: backend.terminate() the current fresh payload, write the durable recipe
command to the tab's own wrapper plus `resume <exact rollout uuid>` (keeping its provider
wrapper, model env and cwd), set status recovery-pending with active recovery intent, then
backend.create_or_resume() and mark running. First attempt used status=stopped and was
correctly refused by TermDeck with "intentionally stopped or archived terminal will not
auto-restart"; recovery-pending is the accepted launchable state.

The applier is idempotent: it re-derives the base command from the stored recipe and strips
any prior " resume " clause before appending exactly one, so re-running cannot double-append.
Verified after the run: 108/108 rows contain a resume clause and 0 rows contain two.

DEFINITIVE VERIFICATION - live process argv, not the registry:
Walked the real process tree of all 108 panes and extracted the UUID following "resume" from
the live argv. Result: 108 of 108 live processes carry exactly the mapped original UUID.
0 wrong UUIDs, 0 panes without a resume argument.
Note: TmuxBackend.recovery_metadata only reported an exact resume command for 22 of 108.
That is a detector limitation, not a recovery failure: resources.observe_recovery_metadata
only recognises a primary rollout owned by the native `codex` / `codex-opencode` process,
and these tabs run through provider proxy wrappers (codex-agnes-proxy.py,
codex-openrouter-proxy.py, codex-hermes-proxy.py) whose node child is not recognised in
that position. Process-argv inspection is the stronger check and is unambiguous here.

  original rollout's 8.86M token / 48 min terminal summary.
- accellion-openrouter shows its findings.md report completion.

- The panes that had been sitting at a Codex folder-trust prompt now load their conversations.

- 108/108 pane cwds match the remembered cwd exactly (0 mismatches).
- t1000 reconcile --dry-run reports changed=0 of 412 (idempotent).
